description_full: Adobe Inc. operates as a technology company worldwide. The Digital Media segment offers products and services that enable individuals, teams, and enterprises to create, publish, and promote content. This segment serves photographers, video editors, graphic and experience designers, game developers, content creators, students, marketers, business owners, knowledge workers, and consumers. The Digital Experience segment provides an integrated platform; and products, services, and solutions that enable brands and businesses to create, manage, execute, measure, monetize, and optimize customer experiences from analytics to commerce. This segment serves marketers, advertisers, agencies, publishers, merchandisers, merchants, web analysts, data scientists, developers, and executives across the C-suite. The Publishing and Advertising segment offers e-learning, technical document publishing, web conferencing, document and forms platform, web application development, printing, and Adobe Advertising solutions. It also provides consulting, training, customer management, technical support, and learning services. The company offers its solutions to enterprise customers, and businesses and consumers; and licenses its products to end-user customers through app stores and website at adobe.com. It markets and distributes its products through distributors, retailers, software developers, mobile app stores, systems integrators, independent software vendors, value-added resellers, and original equipment and hardware manufacturers. The company also provides an online visibility management and content marketing software-as-a-service platform. The company has a strategic alliance with HUMAIN for the development of generative AI models and AI-powered applications. The company was formerly known as Adobe Systems Incorporated and changed its name to Adobe Inc. in October 2018. Adobe Inc. was founded in 1982 and is headquartered in San Jose, California.

financial_summary: Adobe Inc. is a large-cap technology business with a $93.1B market cap on $23.8B of annual revenue.
The top line has compounded at +11% over the past three years and +17% annually across the full decade, a respectable pace for a business of this size.
Returns on capital run at 44% against a 11% cost of capital — a 34-point spread that is the clearest signature of an economic moat. Gross margins of 88% confirm genuine pricing power.

The business throws off $9.9B in free cash flow — roughly 41 cents on every revenue dollar, which is the owner-earnings figure that actually belongs to shareholders, and cash conversion sits at 1.41× so those profits are backed by real cash.
Accruals are elevated at -9.8% of assets, and Sloan showed firms building earnings through accruals rather than cash systematically underperform.
On the balance sheet, the balance sheet carries net cash, which is the gold standard: the business never has to make desperate decisions in a bad year, and interest coverage of 33× is fortress-like.

Management returns a meaningful 12.1% of market cap to owners through dividends and buybacks, a strong signal of disciplined capital allocation, and insider ownership is negligible, so management has little personal stake in the long-term outcome, and within its sector the business captures 1.6× its fair share of profits, a structural advantage visible in the numbers.

sect: Its 37% operating margin runs 30pp above the Technology median (7%), a real cost or pricing edge over peers.
It captures 1.57x its revenue share in sector profits, taking a disproportionate slice of the profit pool.
It accounts for 0.5% of sector revenue and 0.8% of sector operating profit.
Over five years it has been losing share of the sector profit pool (-1.1% a year).
The sector is fragmented and competitive (HHI 0.03 across 530 companies in the universe; the top four hold 29% of revenue), so pricing power is hard to come by.
mkt: The shares are in a steep downtrend, down 27% over the past year excluding the latest month.
The price sits mid-way through its 52-week range, 34% below the high.
With annualised volatility of 41% and a beta of 1.27, it amplifies market moves, though its beta has shifted (1y 0.61 vs 5y 1.37), so read it loosely.
Liquidity is deep, with about $1.1B traded a day.
In past sell-offs it fell 26% in the 2020 crash, 51% in the 2022 bear market and 65% in 2008.
val: The stock trades 44% below its DCF fair value of $425, a meaningful margin of safety.
The fair-value models disagree (dispersion 42%), and the Monte Carlo range runs $327 to $564 (P10-P90), so treat the estimate as noisy.
On multiples it looks cheap against Technology peers: P/E 13.4 vs 26.7, EV/EBITDA 9.8 vs 16.4 and P/FCF 9.5 vs 25.4 (sector median).
Against its own history it is cheap: the EBIT multiple sits 65% below its 10-year median.
Earnings yields are attractive: an FCF yield of 10.6% (above the risk-free rate) and an EBIT/EV of 9.0% (vs the 8% bar).
The 33 covering analysts target $268 on average, 12% above the price, well away from the model's fair value.
prof: ROIC of 44% clears the cost of capital of 10.6% by 34pp, the mark of a value creator; returns have swung a lot from year to year (CV 0.55).
It runs a 88% gross margin and converts 41% of revenue into free cash flow, or 33% after stock compensation.
Earnings quality is mixed: a Piotroski score of 7/9 and cash conversion of 1.41x, but high accruals (-9.8% of assets).
ROE of 61% comes mostly from margins and asset turnover rather than leverage (2.5x equity multiplier).
It spends 8.2% of revenue on stock compensation (above the 2% gate).
hlth: The balance sheet carries net cash of $385.0M (0% of market cap).
No distress or manipulation flags (Altman Z 7.1, in the safe zone).
The current ratio of 1.00 means short-term liabilities exceed current assets.
Goodwill makes up 44% of assets, a soft asset exposed to impairment.
growth: Revenue has compounded at 10.5% over 3 years, 13.1% over 5 years and 17.4% over 10 years, so growth is decelerating.
Net reinvestment is nil (capex and working capital no more than cover depreciation), so fundamental growth is near zero.
Free cash flow has compounded 13.2% a year over five years.
Forward indicators: a book-to-bill of 1.11 (orders outpacing sales), a backlog worth 95% of annual revenue and deferred revenue up 12%.
Capex runs only 0.2x depreciation (0.8% of sales), so the asset base is being harvested rather than grown.
Its Rule of 40 score is 46, clearing the bar for a healthy growth business.
own: Insiders hold little stock (0.2%), and institutions hold 89%.
Insider trading is two-way: 1 purchase and 13 sales over the past year, net $29.5M sold.
It returns 12.1% a year to shareholders (12.1% in buybacks).
The share count has shrunk 3.8% a year over five years, steadily raising each holder's stake.
people: With about 31,360 employees, each generates about $758K of revenue, 2.0x the Technology median, and productivity has risen 13.9% a year.
That works out to $314K of free cash flow per employee.
CEO pay is $5.8M (8x revenue per employee), and compensation governance scores poorly (10/10, lower is better).
